fixture_name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Queue storage and coordination between signalized intersections only ~650 ft apart on a corridor with recorded high-accident designations is a substantive, well-recognized preliminary-design safety issue squarely within FHWA RSA scope.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal 650-ft spacing claim is supported by a verbatim quote from EV-US-001, and the queue-spillback mechanism is transparently labelled as derived inference from that recorded fact rather than invented content.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed purely as a safety_concern with null normative_basis_note and no compliance assertion, correctly preserving the categorical distinction between safety concerns and compliance questions under FHWA RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and viable at preliminary design—signal coordination, Do Not Block Intersection signing, and enhanced display conspicuousness—though it stops short of naming coordination parameters or turn-pocket/storage remedies.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged as crossing both signalized intersections with a reasoned scoping to vehicle occupants based on the spillback mechanism, but VRU-specific effects of retiming (pedestrian phases, crossings blocked by queued vehicles) are not analyzed.
